{{event bar}} {{event boss}} == Rewards == {{anomaly|Entering the [[Queen's Gauntlet]] will hide this event and invalidate your previous participation, requiring you to contribute again to earn the rewards.}} {{event reward table | g-exp = 106680 || g-kar = 1512 || g-coin = 352 | s-exp = 80012 || s-kar = 1136 || s-coin = 264 | b-exp = 53340 || b-kar = 756 || b-coin = 176 }} === Bonus chest === Independent on event participation rewards, one of the following is rewarded based on the meta event completion time: ;Gold Reward Time (all bosses in < 8 minutes) * {{rewards item|Festival Token|qty=80|notes=Gold reward|hide notes=y}} * {{rewards item|Queen's Gauntlet Entrance Ticket|qty=16-20|notes=Gold reward|hide notes=y}} * {{rewards item|Gold Boss Blitz Chest}} ;Silver Reward Time (all bosses in < 16 minutes) * {{rewards item|Festival Token|qty=60|notes=Silver reward|hide notes=y}} * {{rewards item|Queen's Gauntlet Entrance Ticket|qty=11-13|notes=Silver reward|hide notes=y}} * {{rewards item|Silver Boss Blitz Chest}} ;Bronze Reward Time (more than 16 minutes) * {{rewards item|Festival Token|qty=40|notes=Bronze reward|hide notes=y}} * {{rewards item|Queen's Gauntlet Entrance Ticket|qty=7-9|notes=Bronze reward|hide notes=y}} * {{rewards item|Bronze Boss Blitz Chest}} == Walkthrough == In this event, 6 bosses spawn throughout the map, 1 per sector. Event awards are given once all 6 are beaten. Each boss has its own signature ability. Killing a boss transfers that ability to all remaining bosses. This means that an ideal map will kill the bosses within seconds of each other, so their abilities don't persist among the remaining bosses for too long. {| {{STDT|npc}} ! Boss !! Granted ability !! Description !! Tips |- ! [[Sparcus Firesplash]] | {{effect|Fiery Tornado (effect)}} || Dashes to distant players and launches them. Summons [[Fiery Tornado]]es that travel randomly and [[burn]] players who get caught in them. | Sparcus frequently reflects projectiles. Bring weapons and skills that have non-projectile options. When Sparcus dashes, they also summon lava fountains that may be side-stepped. |- ! [[Boom-Boom Baines]] | {{effect|Explosive Powder Keg}} || Throws various grenades that explode after a delay. | Look for and destroy Shielding Turrets to speed up kills. |- ! [[Justiciar Hablion]] | {{effect|Spectral Displacement}} || Summons displacement traps that teleport players to a random place in the sky when triggered. | You do not take fall damage from being displaced. His spinning pull attack may be reflected, which usually fully depletes his defiance bar. |- ! [[Pyroxis]] | {{effect|Firewave}} || Shoots a fan of fire that inflicts [[burning]]. | Its Fireball Barrage attack may be fully reflected, dealing massive significant damage. |- ! [[Wiggin the Wicked]] | {{effect|Bombs Away}} || Sets a field of explosives in a (+) shape that explode after a short delay. | A single dodge can dodge multiple AoE attacks. |- ! [[Kuraii the Cruel]] | {{effect|Trample (Kuraii)}} || Summons a pack of centaurs that roam the battlefield and launch players. | Some of his non-aoe attacks may be reflected. He may be damaged as he runs away. |} ===Strategy=== To achieve a Gold completion rating, all bosses must be defeated within 8 minutes. This time limit is quite lenient and should be easily achievable without coordination. There are two main strategies. ;Strategy that sees frequent use in PUG groups and Multi-map squads # Spread out in groups, equal or unequally amongst 3-5 bosses, leaving Hablion alone. # Engage the bosses, killing them without timing. # The players that kill their bosses early check other bosses' healthbars in the event UI and then go to inactive bosses or the bosses with the most health remaining. # Players end with killing Hablion, as his ability is generally considered the most annoying when passed on. ;Historical strategy that may still see use in organized squads # Separate into 6 roughly even groups close to the start of the event. (During [[Prepare for the Boss Blitz]]) # Engage the boss. When the boss reaches 25% health or lower, reduce your damage. # Check that other groups are reaching the same milestone. Gradually lower their health to around 10%, then halt damage. # Once all groups have reached their 10% milestone, quickly damage your boss and reduce them to 0 health. ;Multi-maps Squad leaders may track multiple instances of Boss Blitz by having certain players "anchor" a map instance. That anchor player stays in that map instance and reports when it is approaching the event start. A squad might have 5 or more instances it is tracking, leading to less downtime between events. When their map event starts, they let the squad know and players will join their instance by right clicking their nameplate in the squad UI. When the event completes the anchor stays and the other players move onto the map that is closest to beginning. ===Tips=== * Generally, maps will request that '''[[Justiciar Hablion]] is killed last'''. This is not mandatory, but is preferred because his ability is the most annoying to deal with. * Every boss features a [[Defiance bar]] mechanic. Breaking the defiance bar will grant {{effect|Might|stacks=5}} to all players not in that pie slice. * Any player who can see a given boss's event is contributing to the scaling of that event, regardless of their participation. This includes dead players and players who are spectating from the bridges that surround the pits. * At the Bronze Tier reward, the bosses no longer transfer their abilities to other bosses once defeated. == Dialogue == ;Talking to [[Blitz Organizer Grayford]] :The Boss Blitz is on! Get out there and fight! :{{dialogue icon|end}} ''All right!'' == Related achievements == * {{achievement|(Annual) Boss Blitz}} * {{achievement|Daily Bonus Rewards: Boss Blitz}} * {{achievement|Boss Blitz|category=Crown Pavilion (achievements)}} == Trivia == * {{event|Defeat Shurakk the Savage}}, [[Legendary Shurakk the Savage]], and the [[ogre]]s were replaced by [[Justiciar Hablion]] and the [[White Mantle]] with [[Festival of the Four Winds 2018]]. ** The six possible [[champion bag]]s rewarded from the tier containers reflect the original enemies, and were not updated. * During August 10 to August 13, 2018, there was a [[Special event]] active. During the Weekend Boss Blitz Bonanza, players had to defeat 5,000 Boss Blitz bosses to earn rewards. Everyone who participated in at least one boss will get 5 {{item icon|Celebration Booster}}s and 10 {{item icon|Zephyrite Supply Box}}es. [https://twitter.com/GuildWars2/status/1028312141621690368] Tweet by @GuildWars2 ** The goal was increased to 7,500 and 10,000 bosses, with additional rewards. The total reward for each player who participated in the weekend event is 25 boosters and 45 boxes. *** However, some players reported receiving the rewards twice. At this moment, it is unknown if it was because of a bug. * The [[Game updates/2025-08-05|August 5, 2025 game update]] ([[Festival of the Four Winds 2025]]) added displays for all bosses' health across the map, allowing easier coordination. == References == {{Festival of the Four Winds nav}} [[Category:Festival of the Four Winds]] [[de:Bossblitz! [[Dragon Arena]] is a [[public instance]] combat arena accessible during [[Dragon Bash]] near {{waypoint|Hero's Compass Waypoint}} where players face off against waves of [[Holographic dragon minion]]s. The waves alternate between a horde of weaker minions, and a champion. In the open world, a [[Holo Mordrem Vinetooth]] fights [[Reveler (Dragon Bash)|Reveler]]s and other NPCs.

There are two types of instances for the Dragon Arena:
* [[File:Dragon Bash.png|24px|link=]] '''Dragon Arena (Public)''' is an open instance that anyone can join, accessed via [[Halstein (Dragon Arena)|Halstein]].
* [[File:Dungeon (map icon).png|24px|link=]] '''Dragon Arena (Private)''' is a 5-man [[dungeon]] instance accessed via a portal northeast of Halstein.
== Dragon Arena (Public) ==
* The public instance supports up to 10 players per map.
* The instance will close after the 6th boss, the Holo Saltspray Dragon, is defeated. Players will be offered two options. They can talk to Halstein to return to Hoelbrak, or volunteer Yes on the standard low map population popup to be placed into another instance of the Dragon Arena.

== Dragon Arena (Private) ==
{{Quotation|game|Test your mettle in the Dragon Arena. Can you survive higher-difficulty holograms?
}}
Dragon Arena (Private) is an alternate version of the instance for 5 players, with additional difficulty settings and the following differences in rules:
* Player characters not standing inside the ice rink will suffer from {{effect|Out of Bounds Penalty}} (10s) every 6 seconds.
* Each Champion Hologram beginning from the first will gain an additional stack of {{effect|Energized Hologram}}. Each stack increases health and damage output.
* At 6 stacks of [[Energized Hologram]] and above, Champion Holograms also gain {{effect|Holographic Strain}}, an effect that pulses unavoidable damage to all foes every 3 seconds. The damage scales with [[Energized Hologram]] stacks, up to around 1,000 per tick at 10 stacks.

== Walkthrough ==
Each Champion Hologram is preceded by a bonus round of endlessly respawning waves of holographic minions. Each five minions defeated grants the entire party 1 stack of {{effect|Bonus Inspiration}}. Players should work together to kill enemies efficiently with area of effect attacks, along with means of grouping enemies, such as [[Spectral Grasp]].

;[[Holo Ice Beast]]
The [[Holo Ice Beast]] will occasionally target a random player character and charge towards them. Getting hit by this attack will cause the character to be flung over the Hologram, while also taking tremendous amounts of damage.

;[[Holo Megadestroyer]]
The Megadestroyer has two main attacks to worry about. The first is a massive punch with a long windup. Getting hit will result in large loss of health, and a knockback. The second is telegraphed by the Megadestroyer standing still, and lava geysers spawning under each player character. The geysers will launch player characters high into the air when it spawns, and deal pulsing damage and fire stacks for a short duration. This second attack can be cut short by breaking the Megadestroyer's defiance.

;[[Holo Branded Hydra]]
The main threat of this fight are the lingering area of effect fields left behind by the Hydra's attacks. Its charging attack — which will always be its opening attack — leaves a trail of purple flame, while the Branded meteors it summons will also leave behind purple rings. Both of these fields deal significant damage each second, as well as apply conditions. At 75% and 25%, a [[Veteran Holo Branded Hydra Head]] will spawn. While mostly harmless, these heads can also create lingering area of effect damage fields.

;[[Holo Mordrem Vinetooth]]
At the beginning of the fight, and every 60s thereafter, the Vinetooth will knock down one player character, while activating its [[defiance]] bar. If its defiance is not broken in time, the Vinetooth will gain a stack of {{effect|Soul Consumption}}, increasing its damage output. Hence, it is necessary to have some crowd control for this fight (approximately 600 points worth). Beyond this, the Vinetooth has some well-telegraphed attacks that should be avoided, where possible.

One of the Eye's main attacks is projectile-based, meaning that groups that can equip some projectile reflecting skills, such as [[Wall of Reflection]] will fare much better than those that don't. Further, the Eye will occasionally channel a long block (indicated by a bright blue glow in front of it). Each attack blocked grants it stacking {{effect|Protection}}, {{effect|Might}}, and {{effect|Resolution}}. Either stop attacking during its blocks, or use boon strips, such as [[Corrupt Boon]].

*A large fireball that splits into two smaller fireballs that each bounce once, appearing as AoE pads on the ground.
*A tornado that spins players around the dragon as lightning strikes in damage pads on the ground. 
*A large strip of fire in front of the dragon.
*Rings of earth as damage pads.
*Ice breath that appears as a cone with three extending pads.
*An S curve of water tornados that appear as damage pads.

{{historical content|Strike Missions were renamed [[Raid Encounters]] and merged with [[Raids]] in the [[Game updates/2026-02-03|February 3, 2026 game update]].}} {{quotation|Official description|Tackle these challenging boss encounters in a group of up to ten players, either as a pre-formed squad or in a public mode anyone can join.}} {{map icon|strike}}[[Strike Mission]]s, or '''strikes''', are 10 player [[squad]]-based [[Player versus Environment|PvE]] [[instance]]s for level 80 [[characters]]. Unlike [[raid]]s, strike missions are repeatable single bossing encounters of characters encountered during the [[Story Journal|story]] with daily rewards. Each encounter typically involves multiple phases with several unique mechanics to test squad coordination, damage output, positioning, and player [[build]]s. Encounters may also include an ''enrage timer'' where the encounter fails when time expires. No [[Mastery|masteries]] are currently required to participate, however some may yield full rewards for select encounters (see table notes). As with raids, [[Downed|downed]] allies can be revived or [[rally]], but [[defeated]] allies cannot be [[Revival|revived]] during the encounters. Unlike [[Fractals of the Mists|fractals]], [[Revive Orb]]s are disabled, along with other similar [[consumable]]s such as [[booster]]s. The first strike mission, [[Strike Mission: Shiverpeaks Pass|Shiverpeaks Pass]], was released on September 17, 2019. This along with the other 6 [[The Icebrood Saga|Icebrood Saga]] strike missions served as an entry point for players into 10-player instanced content. On February 28, 2022, ''[[Guild Wars 2: End of Dragons|End of Dragons]]'' expanded the system by introducing difficulty settings: normal mode, a harder version of the story encounter; and challenge mode, an even harder version with more punishing mechanics.[https://www.guildwars2.com/en-gb/news/guild-wars-2-end-of-dragons-strike-missions/ Guild Wars 2: End of Dragons Strike Missions], GuildWars2.com The [[Strike Mission: Temple of Febe|Temple of Febe]] strike mission from ''[[Guild Wars 2: Secrets of the Obscure|Secrets of the Obscure]]'' introduced a new pinnacle difficulty setting with the legendary mode. == Accessing strike missions== Strike missions are a great introduction to 10-player encounters and common mechanics, bridging the gap between [[open world]] and raid difficulty with some strike missions surpassing raid difficulty. Only the Champions episode of The Icebrood Saga must be unlocked in order to access and start the instances, and it is not required to own the previous Episodes. Completion of the story chapters is also not required as DRM are unlocked immediately upon purchase. == Mechanics == Dragon Response Missions allow both private and public instances, and are structured to have a pre-event, middle progression part, and the end boss encounter. They scale significantly based on the number of players present, meaning they are much more suited for solo play than most other similar instanced content. === Getting started === Public instances use automated matchmaking that lets players join during a pre-event. After its pre-event is done, the instance is locked and from that point functions similarly to a private instance (see below). A help from a random [[#List of Ally Factions|allied faction]] will be assigned at this point. Private instances require a pre-organized [[party]] and function similarly to [[Story Journal|story]] or [[home instance]]s, which means: * Players can only use the [[Looking For Group|LFG]] tool prior to starting the instance as party member slots are locked upon entering. * Before starting, it is important to have all party members to be in the same [[Eye of the North]] [[instance]]. Players that are in a different instance will not get any invitation from the instance initiator. * Only initiating player can cancel the mission start as they are technically considered to be the instance owner. This is useful to prevent starting the instance prior to all members accepting mission invitation. * Other party members, non-initiators, can only accept or reject the mission invitation. If non-initiators reject, they will be left behind in the Eye of the North, while any accepting member will be launched into the mission instance. Players who joined the party later similarly will be unable to enter the mission. * If a player was disconnected, they will be unable to rejoin the ongoing mission. The only way to let a such player in is for the entire group to leave the instance and restart it from the Eye of the North. Private instances allow activating challenges for achievements ([[Champions (achievements)|Champions]] category) and extra rewards by speaking with {{vendor|misc|Event flag red (map icon).png}} [[Veadh]] at the start. Players can also enlist the support of a specific allied faction from {{vendor|misc|Event flag blue (map icon).png}} [[Meradh]] at the cost of {{currency|10|Tyrian Defense Seal|text=yes}}s. === General mission structure === [[File:Dragon Response Mission preparation phase objectives.png|Objectives of preparation phase in [[Dragon Response Mission: Gendarran Fields]].|thumb|right]] During the preparation phase, there are up to three tasks, one of which is always defeating a certain number of enemies in the area. Other tasks vary from building defenses and other structures to arming allies, running supplies, putting out fires, or saving locals by talking to them. * Saving locals is done by talking to them, which will make them follow you until you reach their drop-off zone. Until you drop them off they will not count for progressing that task. These NPCs cannot be killed and will follow you on any mount. * Progressing any task will contribute to the stability progress bar. Any task completed will grant a {{effect|Morale Boost (Dragon Response Mission)|Morale Boost}} for the rest of the mission. * Once the stability progress bar fills up, the mission is immediately progressed towards the middle part. For the middle part, complete the task given, usually either a defense event of a certain area from 5 waves of enemies, escorting the NPCs to the boss location, or a combination of both. The final part of each mission is a boss fight. Each boss has its own mechanics – see individual mission pages for details. {{item icon|Potion of Destroyer Slaying}} and {{item icon|Potion of Ice Brood Slaying}} are usable and provide their bonuses inside the corresponding Dragon Response Missions. === Achievements and challenges === Completing the mission with a challenge activated and an eligible Allied Faction either randomised or recruited from {{vendor|misc|Event flag blue (map icon).png}} Meradh awards progress to the mission's respective {{achievement icon|Champions (achievements)#achievement5688|Tide Turner}} achievement. == Mechanics ==
=== Locating Rifts ===
* Rifts appear throughout the [[Tyria (world)|world of Tyria]]:
** [[Kryptis]] [[Mists Rift (Kryptis)|Mists Rifts]] can always be found in [[Horn of Maguuma]].
** Kryptis rifts will open in several other [[zone]]s on a weekly cycle, which are listed in-game in the {{achievement icon|Weekly Rift Hunting}} achievement category.
** [[Titan]]spawn [[Mists Rift (Titanspawn)|Mists Rifts]] can always be found in [[Janthir]].
** [[Inquest]], [[choya]], and [[seer]] defenses [[Mists Rift (Castora)|Mists Rifts]] can be found in [[Castora]].
* Using the {{skill icon|Scan for Rift|size=18}} [[mastery skill]] in an active map to locate an active rift.
** The default [[keybind]] for ''Activate Mastery Skill'' is {{key|J}}, and a unique keybind can be set to ''[[Scan for Rift]]'' in the [[Options#Control Options|Control Options]] menu.
** Using the skill will show particles around your character that flow in the direction of the rift. If the rift event is already active, it will be displayed on your screen and the area will be circled in red on your map.
** If you use the skill in a zone without active rifts, you will be shown a list of active maps.

=== Closing Rifts ===
* Upon interacting with a rift with the [[Heart of the Obscure]], a pre-event will start which requires you to kill lesser minions that begin spawning in the area.
* There are two types of rifts:
** Most rifts will require you to kill a certain number of enemies to progress.
** Rifts in [[Inner Nayos]] and some in [[Castora]] require you to defend the rift for 3 minutes, preventing enemies from escaping through it. If enough enemies escape, the event will fail.
* After the pre-event, a single player will have to interact with the rift again with the Heart of the Obscure or a Rift Motivation to begin the fight with an [[elite]] (for Tier 1) or [[champion]] (for Tier 2 and 3) enemy.
* The rift can be closed with the Heart of the Obscure after killing the final enemy.
* There is no cooldown for Rift Hunting, so another can be sought out after closing one.

=== Motivations and Rift Tiers ===
* There are 3 tiers of rifts. The first and easiest tier is, by default, intended to be completable by a solo player. Higher tiers are scaled for groups by default.
* One of each tier of rifts exist simultaneously in a single zone instance, all tracked separately. By default only tier 1 rifts are tracked. Use/activate a "Motivation" item in your inventory to grant an effect that changes the tier of rift [[Scan for Rift]] will track. Doing this ''does not'' spend the motivation item.
** Motivations can be crafted after unlocking the appropriate [[Secrets of the Obscure mastery tracks#Astral Ward|Astral Ward mastery]] and buying the recipe, e.g. from [[Lyhr]] in [[The Wizard's Tower]]. They can also be traded with other players on the [[Trading Post]].
** {{item icon|Fine Rift Motivation}} - Re-toggles tracking tier 1 rifts if another rift tier has been toggled.
** {{item icon|Masterwork Rift Motivation}}  - Toggles tracking tier 2 rifts.
** {{item icon|Rare Rift Motivation}}  - Toggles tracking tier 3 rifts.
* When you interact with the rift after finishing the pre-event, you can use a common motivation instead of the Heart of the Obscure for the rift T1, which increases the rewards you'll get for completing the rift. For the rifts T2 and T3, at least one of the participants needs to use a motivation of appropriate tier to open it. If you decide to apply the motivation, select the corresponding line in the interaction dialog:
:{{dialogue icon|combat}} ''Use a [[Fine Rift Motivation|common motivation]] to draw additional Kryptis essence.'' — for rift T1
:{{dialogue icon|combat}} ''Use a ([[Masterwork Rift Motivation|uncommon]], [[Rare Rift Motivation|rare]]) motivation to draw out the Kryptis.'' — for rifts T2 and T3

:Doing this ''will'' spend the motivation item.
* Spending {{item icon|Fine Rift Motivation}}s on tier 1 rifts is optional; they can be opened without one by using the Heart of the Obscure, but it increases your personal rewards. Higher tier rifts require that at least one player spends a motivation item of the given tier in order to open them. Other players then have several seconds during which they can (but don't have to) spend their own motivations as well to increase their rewards from the event.
* Players may receive rewards from participating in pre-events and rift closures even if they do not own, or have not started, the Secrets of the Obscure story. However, these players will not be able to open rifts, spawn the elite or champion enemy, or close the rift (since doing so requires access to the Heart of the Obscure).
